column1: # Complete original-test evidence for the connected mutable-transaction runtime.

column8: The complete original helper-store and batch-merge file remains covered and is retained beside the new live MemBufferDriver consumer.
The exact a-through-d buffer, middle, snapshot, tombstone, missing-key, cardinality, and layer-specific ReturnCommitTS fixture remains covered through the single merge authority.

Every transaction test target is deterministic and owns or explicitly closes its iterators; Go SetupForCommonTest and its process-wide goleak allowlist remain harness-specific and are not claimed as Rust runtime equivalence.

The focused Rust targets complete without background workers by construction and exercise explicit iterator closure, while the five Go goleak ignore functions and Bazel timeout hook remain external test-harness obligations.
The complete original merge, error, and close behavior remains covered and is consumed unchanged by the mutable transaction runtime.
All four record tables remain exact in forward and reverse order, including snapshot-only, dirty-only, override, tombstone suppression, and either input exhausting first.
All nine constructor and Next error cases retain exact error identity, dirty-before-snapshot advancement, caller ownership after constructor failure, and explicit close-both semantics.

All three original declarations remain translated through one transaction driver, now with a source-shaped injected mutable buffer; concrete mockstore begin/commit and client lifecycle remain external.

Snapshot and commit-ts reads, dirty replace/insert, deletion and missing identities, and post-interceptor dirty/deleted/snapshot precedence remain exact; MemBufferDriver additionally supplies the live source-shaped mutation boundary, while Go value-plus-error shape and concrete mockstore remain open.

Snapshot-only and mixed batch reads, commit timestamps, dirty overrides and tombstones, missing omission, buffer-only reads, and interceptor errors remain exact through the canonical merge; nil-map-plus-error and request context remain open.

All original bounds, dirty mutations, merged forward/reverse scans, and interceptor failure remain exact; the new runtime test proves the same path receives MemBufferDriver iterators and prefix mutations, while concrete TiKV scanning remains external.

The complete original prefix file remains covered, including empty and populated deletion, true/false scans, embedded-NUL filtering, error cleanup, tombstone suppression, and byte-boundary regressions.

The exact prefix scan/delete vectors, empty and populated deletion, unrelated-key preservation, tombstone suppression, cleanup, and byte-boundary regressions remain covered by the source-focused prefix suite; mutable_transaction_runtime_source.rs additionally executes the same authority through the injected MemBufferDriver over committed snapshot and dirty keys.
The exact embedded-NUL child-prefix false case and unrelated-key true case remain covered by the sole inverted-prefix predicate.
